title: The 3/8 Exponent for Shortest Directed Paths
description: In a KMSW cell encoded by n independent uniform steps from {(1, −1), (−1, 0), (0, 1)}, let Δn be the largest finite shortest directed-path distance, measured in edges. Every median mn of Δn satisfies mn = n3/8+o(1).
description_html: In a KMSW cell encoded by n independent uniform steps from {(1, −1), (−1, 0), (0, 1)}, let Δ<sub>n</sub> be the largest finite shortest directed-path distance, measured in edges. Every median m<sub>n</sub> of Δ<sub>n</sub> satisfies m<sub>n</sub> = n<sup>3/8+o(1)</sup>.

title: Graph Limits of Longest Directed Paths
description: For the uniform infinite bipolar-oriented triangulation, rescale north- and west-going exploration times by n and longest directed-path lengths by n3/4. The resulting fields are tight, and every subsequential closed-graph limit is almost surely a locally bounded continuous function on the limiting domain of directed-comparable edge pairs.

The resulting fields are tight, and every subsequential closed-graph limit is almost surely a locally bounded continuous function on the limiting domain of directed-comparable edge pairs.

title: Nontrivial Limits of Shortest Directed Paths
description: For the uniform infinite bipolar-oriented triangulation, rescale exploration times by n and shortest directed-path lengths by the upper integer median of the maximal finite distance in an n-step KMSW cell. Subsequential closed-graph limits are continuous functions. In limits taken jointly with the primal and dual peanosphere data, the function is almost surely not identically zero.

title: Mesh-Only Convergence for Orthogonal Tilings
description: For orthogonal tilings in dimension d ≥ 2 with mesh ε → 0, discrete harmonic extensions of smooth harmonic boundary data converge uniformly without the original theorem’s additional geometric alternatives. For h harmonic and C2 near a bounded domain compactly inside the tiled region, the supplement gives error ≤ C‖h‖C² ε4/(d+4), hence exponent 2/3 in the plane. Harmonic measures and stopped walks also converge, with walks considered modulo time parametrization.

title: Sphere Packings and Tangency-Polytope Tilings
description: For every nonempty open Ω ⊂ ℝd, d ∈ {2, 3, 4}, there is a packing by arbitrarily small balls whose tangency polytopes form a locally finite, face-to-face tiling of exactly Ω. Ball tangencies correspond precisely to shared facets. Each tile has at most 6, 12, or 24 facets in dimensions 2, 3, or 4, respectively.

title: Sphere Averages in Odd Dimensions
description: For odd d = 2m + 1 ≥ 3, the spherical-average process St = he⁻ᵗ(0) − h1(0) of a log-correlated Gaussian field has an explicit Brownian convolution representation. Its paths are locally Cm−1,α for every α < 1, but it has no mth mean-square derivative.

Its paths are locally C<sup>m−1,α</sup> for every α < 1, but it has no mth mean-square derivative.

title: Quantum Cones in Odd Dimensions
description: For odd d ≥ 3, 0 < γ < √(2d), and β < Q = d/γ + γ/2, recentering the spherical-average process at its first crossing of −b after subtracting (Q − β)t gives a total-variation limit on each fixed radial tail as b → ∞. The associated rescaled fields converge locally in total variation to a β-quantum cone.

title: Reflected Random Walks with Spatial Singularities
description: Under the stated connectivity, mass-transport, ergodicity, and finite-moment assumptions on a planar cell environment, the reflected walk with area-over-conductance holding times converges diffusively, for almost every environment, to Brownian motion with deterministic positive-definite covariance. The main note permits a closed singular set of zero one-dimensional Hausdorff measure; the companion treats whole-plane coverings with connectivity along almost every horizontal and vertical line.

title: An Axiomatic Metric in Higher Dimensions
description: Proposed theorem: for d ≥ 3 and Q(ξ) > √(2d), the whole-space log-correlated Gaussian field admits a metric satisfying the length-space, locality, Weyl-scaling, and translation–dilation axioms. These axioms determine the metric up to a deterministic positive constant.

title: Conformal Covariance of Supercritical LQG
description: For ξ > ξcrit, a fixed deterministic conformal bijection φ: U → V, and h a GFF plus a continuous function on V, almost surely Dh(φ(u), φ(v); V) = Dh∘φ + Q log|φ′|(u, v; U) simultaneously for all u, v ∈ U, including singular endpoints.

title: The Small-γ LQG Dimension Expansion
description: Proposed asymptotic: dγ = 2 + kγ4/3 + o(γ4/3) as γ ↓ 0, for a deterministic k ∈ (0, ∞). The coefficient is characterized by a Gaussian variational limit; its numerical value is not evaluated.

title: Gaussian Fluctuations of LQG Distance
description: Proposed theorem: for a whole-plane GFF normalized by h1(0) = 0, normalize the metric so the median global left–right distance across the unit square is one. Then (Dhγ(0, 1) − 1)/γ converges in law to N(−q/2, 3/8), where q < 0 is the median of the minimum, over y ∈ [0, 1], of ∫01 h(x + iy) dx. The line integrals are defined by L2 limits.

The line integrals are defined by L<sup>2</sup> limits.

title: Higher-Dimensional LFPP Exponents
description: For every fixed d ≥ 2 and sufficiently small ξ > 0, the LFPP exponent λd(ξ) = 1 − ξQd(ξ) satisfies cd ξ4/3/log(1/ξ) ≤ λd(ξ) ≤ Cd ξ4/3. Consequently λd(ξ) = ξ4/3+o(1).

title: Tightness of Small-Parameter Geodesics
description: Let Pγ be the LQG geodesic from 0 to 1 in a whole-plane GFF, parametrized at constant metric speed on [0, 1]. The paths t ↦ γ−2/3(Pγ(t) − t) are tight in C([0, 1], ℝ2) as γ ↓ 0.

title: Two-Thirds Geodesic Deviation
description: Let Mγ be the maximum Euclidean distance from [0, 1] reached by the whole-plane LQG geodesic from 0 to 1. Then Mγ/γ2/3 is tight and bounded away from zero in probability as γ ↓ 0. Quantitatively, 𝔼Mγ ≤ Cγ2/3 and ℙ[Mγ ≤ aγ2/3] ≤ Ca3/5 for 0 < a ≤ 1 and sufficiently small γ.

Quantitatively, 𝔼M<sub>γ</sub> ≤ Cγ<sup>2/3</sup> and ℙ[M<sub>γ</sub> ≤ aγ<sup>2/3</sup>] ≤ Ca<sup>3/5</sup> for 0 < a ≤ 1 and sufficiently small γ.
